# NIKL article 44: separate nonzero myriad groups; compact is a customer option.
# unit (a space after every Sino unit) and digits spaced form the opt-in
# Korean scale arithmetic and counter reading policies
# Counters that take native numerals in standard Korean. Without a row the
# number falls through to the sino numeral, so 2쌍 read 이쌍 instead of 두 쌍.
# Keep numeric calendar/scale markers pending across phrase boundaries.
# Atomic major scales; their reading labels remain in magnitude resources.
# Exact attached quantity tails; no arbitrary particle-prefix word matching.
# Financial quantities retain their written unit and exact decimal value.
# Written meridiem suffix and language-specific rendering.
# A range reads the unit once, after the second number (3~5kg 삼에서 오 킬로그램;
# AI Hub 159 references 1466:6). customers/range-repeat-unit restores both units.
# Adjacent approximate numbers contract (2~3만 원 이삼만 원, 3~4개 서너 개,
# 20~30명 이삼십 명; references 663:172 for digits, 463:108 for tens).
# Written currency names use the same semantic units as currency symbols.
# An exact hour drops its zero minutes (09:00 → 아홉 시); set read to keep them.
# A bracketed weekday marks a slash date: 5/8(수). Used only as a date cue.
# Calendar and clock units written across tokens (3월 1일~3월 5일) are one scale;
# a range between two of them is not a quantity interval.
# Rendering of DATE/weekday identities, shared with source language packs.
# A number inside a fixed name is read as the name says: the disease name
# 코로나19 is 코로나 일구, never 코로나 십구. The spaced count 코로나 19명 is unaffected.
# Latin unit letters attached to a number in a Korean sentence (speech output):
# 75t급 -> 칠십오 톤급, 3,000P -> 삼천 포인트, 4Km -> 사 킬로미터. Korean only; shared
# numeric_suffix is language neutral and p means pence or page in English.
